title: Praise the process, never the person
statement: Praise and encouragement name the specific process or strategy the learner used, never the person, stay truthful and never slip in the answer.
detail: The grade-3 rulebook's register with the child says to praise the process, never the person, never to praise effort on something easy, and never to make points or praise the reason to read. A reading quality canon asks that uptake name the strategy the child used, as in 'I like how you used what you know about lions to decide…', praising the process, not the answer.
against: A grade 9 lesson engine gives every line a student reads one plain voice with no praise at all (the record one-plain-voice-for-every-line), so whether a line may praise differs between courses; the two fit only when the encouragement names an effort or strategy rather than praising. Untested with students.

evidence.quote: Praise the PROCESS, never the person; never praise effort on something easy.
The reason to read stays inside the text — points and praise are never the reason.
Uptake names the strategy the child used ('I like how you used what you know about lions to decide…'), praising the process not the answer.
Motivator: encourage a specific useful effort or strategy, without giving away the answer.
The Motivator supports persistence through specific, truthful encouragement without quietly supplying the interpretation.
Helps students re-engage without doing the reasoning for them. Encouragement should remain truthful and age-appropriate.
